description: Create a tracked ISSUES.md issue registry at the repo root capturing every issue found across the review rounds (the v1 semantic review's four issues plus any UI issues found by Playwright in FEAT-005), then autonomously resolve the resolvable ones in code and record the resolution/justification for each. This provides the orchestrator with ready-to-file GitHub Issues and demonstrates the review -> issue -> fix loop the user asked for. (The orchestrator files the actual GitHub Issues and pushes; this agent cannot run gh/push.)
steps: Create ISSUES.md at the repo root. For each issue use a clear format: a stable id (ISSUE-1, ISSUE-2, ...), title, severity, source (which review round / Playwright / which review file), description, and a Status field (Open / Fixed / Won't fix with justification) plus the commit or files that resolved it. Seed it from the v1 review file in .agents/tasks/task-mlb-postseason-site/ (the four issues: series-ID contract across seed/live boundary; Bedrock path unverifiable offline; no infra tests; BucketDeployment prune/config.js interaction) and any UI issues recorded by FEAT-005.

RESOLVE ISSUE: Series-ID contract across seed/live boundary. In the backend, make prediction lookup robust: in bracketService.getPrediction, if an exact series-id match is not found, fall back to resolving by parsing the id (season-league-round-highId-lowId) and matching on round + the unordered team-id pair, so a high/low-seed ordering disagreement between the live aggregation and the bundled seed does not 404. Add/extend a backend vitest to assert that a prediction for a series whose high/low are swapped relative to the stored bracket still resolves. Keep the existing SeriesNotFoundError for genuinely unknown series.

RESOLVE ISSUE: No infra tests. Add infra/test/stack.test.ts using aws-cdk-lib/assertions Template.fromStack to assert: the DynamoDB table has a TTL spec and pk key; both Lambda functions exist with Node 20 runtime and TABLE_NAME + BEDROCK_MODEL_ID env; the prediction function's role has an IAM policy allowing bedrock:InvokeModel; the HTTP API has the three routes; CloudFront has the SPA error responses; and both bucket deployments exist. Add vitest (or the infra workspace's test runner) wiring so `npm test -w infra` runs it. Ensure it runs without any live AWS call (synth-time assertions only).

RESOLVE ISSUE: BucketDeployment prune / config.js. In the CDK stack, make config.js robust against the SPA deployment's prune so it is never transiently absent: either (a) add an explicit dependency so the runtime-config deployment runs after the SPA deployment and exclude /config.js from the SPA deployment's managed objects, or (b) write config.js as part of the same single BucketDeployment via Source.data so there is only one deployment and no prune race. Document the chosen approach in a code comment and in ISSUES.md. Re-run cdk synth to confirm the template still builds.

ADDRESS ISSUE: Bedrock path unverifiable offline. This cannot be fully verified without live AWS, so it is not code-fixable here. In code, add a focused unit test for RealBedrockInvoker that mocks the BedrockRuntimeClient send() to return a realistic Anthropic messages response body and asserts the request body shape (anthropic_version, max_tokens, messages) and the content[].text parsing - this guards the request/response shaping that was previously only covered by the higher-level mock. In ISSUES.md mark the remaining live-verification step as a documented post-deploy smoke test (not resolvable in this environment) with clear instructions.
Address any UI issues from FEAT-005 that were not already fixed within FEAT-005, or confirm in ISSUES.md that they were fixed there.
Update ISSUES.md Status for each issue to Fixed (with the resolving files/commit) or Won't-fix-with-justification (for the live-only Bedrock smoke test). Keep the registry accurate.

Run the full verification: `npm run build`, `npm test` (all workspaces incl. new backend + infra tests), and `npm run synth`. Confirm all pass with no live AWS calls. Commit with a message referencing the issues resolved so progress is visible in git history.
acceptance_criteria: ISSUES.md exists at the repo root listing every issue with id, title, severity, source, description, and status; each issue is either Fixed (with resolving files) or Won't-fix with a written justification.
Backend prediction lookup resolves a series by round + unordered team pair when an exact id match fails, with a vitest asserting the swapped-high/low case resolves instead of 404ing.

infra/ has a Template.fromStack assertion test covering DynamoDB TTL/key, both Lambdas (Node 20 + env vars), the Bedrock InvokeModel IAM policy, the HTTP API routes, and the bucket deployments; `npm test -w infra` runs it and passes with no live AWS call.
The CDK config.js injection is made robust against the SPA deployment prune (single deployment via Source.data, or explicit ordering + exclusion), verified by `cdk synth`.

A unit test asserts RealBedrockInvoker's Anthropic request body shape and content[].text response parsing against a mocked BedrockRuntimeClient; the remaining live Bedrock verification is documented in ISSUES.md as a post-deploy smoke test.
`npm run build`, `npm test`, and `npm run synth` all pass at the repo root with no live AWS calls.
verification: From repo root: `npm test` exits 0 (backend, frontend, infra tests all pass).
From repo root: `npm run build` exits 0.
From repo root: `npm run synth` exits 0 and writes the CloudFormation template.
Confirm ISSUES.md exists at repo root and every listed issue has a resolved/justified status.
findings:
FEAT-006 COMPLETE and VERIFIED (no live AWS). ISSUES.md registry created at repo root with 5 tracked issues (ISSUE-1..5), each with id/title/severity/source/description/status + resolving files.

== VERIFICATION (all exit 0, no live AWS/Bedrock calls) ==
- `npm run build` (root): shared+backend+frontend+infra all compile.
- `npm test` (root): backend 25 tests, frontend 12 tests, infra 6 tests all pass.
- `npm run synth` (root): cdk synth builds MlbPostseasonStack.template.json; config.js content present (Source.data marker '<<marker:0xbaba:0>>' bundled into the single deployment asset) and exactly ONE Custom::CDKBucketDeployment resource in the template.

== RESOLUTIONS ==
ISSUE-1 (series-id contract) FIXED: backend/src/service/bracketService.ts gained parseSeriesId + roundSlugOf + resolveSeries; getPrediction now resolves exact id first, then falls back to round-slug + unordered team-pair match, preserving SeriesNotFoundError for genuine misses. Tests in bracketService.test.ts assert swapped high/low id (2024-al-wildcard-116-117 -> stored 2024-al-wildcard-117-116) resolves, and an unknown pair still 404s. (8 service tests pass.)
ISSUE-2 (Bedrock path) FIXED (shaping) + WON'T-FIX-HERE (live smoke): RealBedrockInvoker already accepted an injectable BedrockRuntimeClient (no refactor needed). narrative.test.ts adds a describe block injecting a stubbed send() returning a realistic Anthropic body and asserting (a) InvokeModelCommand request shape (anthropic_version/max_tokens/temperature/messages, modelId/contentType/accept) and (b) content[].text parse + concatenation + no-text error. Residual live post-deploy smoke test documented in ISSUES.md (curl /prediction, expect 200 + non-fallback model) - not runnable offline.
ISSUE-3 (no infra tests) FIXED: infra/test/stack.test.ts uses aws-cdk-lib/assertions Template.fromStack (fixed env, no live AWS) asserting DynamoDB TTL(ttl)+pk HASH, two nodejs20.x app Lambdas with TABLE_NAME+BEDROCK_MODEL_ID (via resourcePropertiesCountIs=2 since CDK adds helper Lambdas), bedrock:InvokeModel IAM policy, GET /bracket + GET/POST /prediction routes, CloudFront 403/404 CustomErrorResponses, and exactly 1 Custom::CDKBucketDeployment. infra already had vitest devDep + `vitest run` test script; tsconfig include extended to test/**/*.ts. `npm test -w infra` passes (6).
ISSUE-4 (BucketDeployment prune race) FIXED: infra/lib/mlb-postseason-stack.ts now ships the SPA asset + Source.data('config.js') in ONE DeploySpa BucketDeployment (removed separate DeployRuntimeConfig), so prune is internally consistent and /config.js is never transiently absent. Choice documented in a code comment; infra test asserts single-deployment count.
ISSUE-5 (mobile bracket overflow) already FIXED in FEAT-005 (styles.css <=560px single-column); recorded as Fixed in ISSUES.md.
